vehicle. unit 1 driver informed me that he was traveling [roadway] [roadway] 410 eb when unit 2 walked in front of him. unit 2 was traveling on foot in an area that pedestrians are prohibited from the body.

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was traveling northbound [roadway]. unit 1 driver admitted to driving at speeds up to 80 mph in a 75 mph zone while it was raining and the roadway was wet. unit 2 was [roadway] and began [roadway] while slowing its speed. unit 2 was slowing down and moving over for unit 3. unit 3, a rollback wrecker, which was parked with its rollback fully extended with its emergency warning lights on, was [roadway] and the west-side shoulder. unit 1 driver gave the investigating officer consent to search her call/text history. unit 1 driver accepted a face time call one minute prior to the crash. unit 1 failed to slow down or move over for unit 3. unit 1 failed to control speed and crashed into the rear left side of unit 2, with its front right. the pedestrian wrecker driver was utilizing his outboard cable switch, located on unit 3's rear driver side. after crashing into unit 2, unit 1 drove up on unit 3's extended rollback. unit 1 front undercarriage crashed into the pedestrian wrecker driver as unit 1 vaulted off the rollback of unit 3. after becoming airborne, unit 1 came to rest in the median, upright, facing west. unit 2 came to rest north of the bridge, facing north, on the improved shoulder. unit 3 remained parked and stationary throughout the crash. the pedestrian wrecker driver came to rest behind unit 3 driver side second axle, facing northeast. unit 1 driver was initially arrested for failed to slow/move over for certain stationary vehicles causing serious bodily injury. the pedestrian later succumbed to his injuries. unit 1 driver has been charged with negligent homicide. the case has been forwarded to the freestone county district attorneys office for prosecution. disposition pending.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date], at approx 0617, i, off fulcher, was notified of a crash at the durham transportaton parking lot near our office. chief humphrey advised that it was a pedestrian vs a vehicle and ems was already en-route. i arrived on scene at 0628. the pedestrian, lessie williams, was being loaded into an ambulance. i made contact with the driver of the vehicle, faith evans about the incident and took her information. faith advised, she was pulling into the parking lot when the crash occurred. she advised that she is a tdy bus driver. she advised she was pulling forward in order to backup into a parking spot when she heard a loud thud on her vehicle. she then advised she never saw lessie until she got out of the vehicle after striking her. faith advised she was not ill, intoxicated, fatigued, or on any medication that would affect her driving. she advised she was not injured in the crash and was wearing her safety belt at the time. at approximately 0710, [medical facility] to make contact with lessie. she advised she was walking across the parking lot from her vehicle to the bus barn so she could clock in. she advised she saw faith approaching in her vehicle, she advised she figured faith saw her walking across the parking lot. she initially advised the rear of faith's vehicle struck her. video footage later showed lessie was struck bu the front end of faiths vehicle. nurses advised they were doing x rays to determine the extent of lessie's injuries. lessie advised however, that she already had a large lump on the top of her head from where she hit the ground upon being struck by the vehicle. i advised lessie and her daughter cindy to update our department once the extent of her injuries was determined. lessie advised she was not ill, intoxicated, fatigued, or on any medication that would affect her alertness. i reviewed the security camera footage. the crash can be seen on two separate cameras. faith enters the parking lot at 06:07:57 and the crash occurs at 06:08:14. i added a disc to this case that contains a three minute segment of both camera views and pictures from the scene. at approximately 1234, i made contact with donald songer (w/m dob: [date] bus driver) he was near the scene in his bus and witnessed the crash. he gave a written statement which advised the following: ""i looked out my bus windshield and saw a white suv hit lessie williams and knock her backwards in the air. i got off my bus and ran to assist lessie williams. the driver of the suv was also out of her car by the time i arrived. i did not see lessie williams approach the suv. the point i saw the accident is when lessie was thrown backwards. her cell phone was about 10-15 feet from her. i picked it up and gave it to jan-office personnel. when i got to lessie williams her feet were under the bumper of the suv and she was shoeless. one shoe was under the suv. i don't know where the other one was. ""

[date] corrections: the driver of unit 1's address was corrected from [roadway]. and the charge of ""hit and run"" was changed to driving while license invalid.

records.deidentified_narrative: driver of unit 1 said she was on wrangler, and turned east onto country club. she said she saw no one, but then heard a noise, and realized she had hit something, so she stopped, and indicated she initially stopped about 10-15 ft from the intersection, east of wrangler on country club. driver realized she had struck the pedestrian and his dog. cosa ambulance had transported the pedestrian away from the scene with his dog. pedestrian said he was walking westbound on country club approaching wrangler, on [roadway], walking his dog. he said unit 1 came from wrangler, and did a ""rolling stop"", then turned, and struck him and his dog. pedestrian said he was struck by the passenger side of the vehicle, and that his dog was struck and rolled up under the driver side of the vehicle. i asked pedestrian to approximate his location in relation to the intersection and he provided what is shown on the diagram- out of the intersection to the east. i looked for any indication, but was unable to find anything to independently determine poi. i noted dog hair on unit 1 front left tire. i noted a crack in the bumper/plastic on front left of unit 1, indicating the dog impact on that side. i noted some disturbance (dust and dew) on the front of the vehicle and towards the passenger side, which may have been where pedestrian impacted the vehicle. pedestrian had scrape on right knee, and face. pedestrian's dog may have broken leg. there was dew on the grass, and so i was able to determine that unit 1 was not driving off the paved roadway, and had not cut the corner of the intersection into the vegetation in the turn. there was a puddle of water on wrangler near the intersection, but multiple vehicles had driven through and i was not able to determine wet tire tracks for unit 1.

records.public_safe_text: driver of unit #1 [roadway] at the [roadway]. driver of unit #1 said he had a red light as he was stopped at the intersection. driver of unit #1 said he looked right and left to make sure he was able to make a right turn into the sb lanes of 121. driver of unit #1 said as he began to make the right turn he slightly struck the pedestrian causing him to fall. officer spoke to the pedestrian and he said he only remembered falling and denied being struck by a vehicle. the pedestrians son arrived shortly after and said the pedestrian suffered from a severe case of dementia. the pedestrian left the residence unsupervised at the time of the crash. officer was unable to get any further information from the pedestrian as a result of his dementia. officer stood at the sw crosswalk where a traffic control device is provided to the pedestrian. the device requires that a pedestrian press the crosswalk button in order to activate. once activated the control device allows 15 seconds for a pedestrian to cross. officer was unable to determine if the pedestrian activated the device. officer saw no cameras in the area that could aid in the investigation. witness: yan chun [phone], said she was behind unit #1 at the time of the accident and said the light for unit #1 was red and turned green when she saw the pedestrian get struck. officer took pictures and uploaded them into evidence. com.
